title: Session-pinned canary with deterministic shadow replay and graceful drain
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: reduce noisy user-visible regressions during canary promotions by ensuring session-affine traffic stays pinned while enabling deterministic shadow replay for offline verification before promotion. This PR implements a session-pinned canary lane that pins user sessions to the incumbent variant until a session-safe handoff completes and introduces a deterministic shadow replay path that replays sampled live requests into candidate models with preserved session state. Key goals: maintain session consistency for stateful flows, provide reproducible shadow results for automated regression detectors, and support graceful drain with end-to-end idempotency guarantees. Design summary: 1) Session affinity tokens: requests now carry a stable session token used by the canary conductor to decide pinning eligibility. 2) Handoff protocol: a three-phase handshake (prepare, verify, commit) that verifies KV-cache compatibility and replay parity before committing session transfers. 3) Deterministic shadow replay: captured request + session KV is replayed through the candidate in a deterministic executor that disables non-deterministic hooks and seeds RNGs. Replays are recorded to the shadow-results store for batch evaluation. 4) Graceful drain and rewind: if a safety gate trips, affected sessions are rewound to incumbent within the same flow using snapshot checkpointing. 5) Metrics and telemetry: new histograms for replay-latency, replay-diff-score, and session-handoff-duration; integrated into console rollout dashboard. Checklist: - [x] core conductor protocol and handshake implementation - [x] deterministic executor and replay capture - [x] session snapshotting and rewind hooks - [x] telemetry, tracing spans, and dashboard wiring - [x] unit and e2e smoke tests - [x] rollout playbook and runbook entry Backwards compatibility: falls back to existing stateless canaries when session tokens are absent. Migration notes: to enable session-pinned canaries an operator flag must be set and a short config migration on Dedicated clusters performed to enable checkpoint storage. Security: session tokens are treated as opaque identifiers and not logged; replay store encrypted with existing KMS keys. Commit summary: small focused commits for protocol and tests followed by a squash for release. See commits below. CI: flaky integration test (replay-suite) retried once; all checks passed on final run. Merge strategy: squash and merge. Impact: primarily rollout conductor and runtime executor changes; rollout safety gates tightened. Release notes: Adds session-aware canaries and deterministic shadow replay for safer model promotions, enabled via operator flag. No breaking API changes.

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: The handshake looks solid but we need to ensure the prepare phase has a timeout so we don't block on stuck sessions. Can we also add an audit span for prepare/verify/commit?
Maya Chen: Added prepare timeout with configurable default 30s. Added tracing spans for each phase and surfaced them in console. See commit d9910ff and f3a8a11.
Priya Natarajan: The deterministic executor disables a few runtime optimizations. We should document the performance tradeoffs and ensure replay sampling rate is conservative by default.
Maya Chen: Documented tradeoffs in protocol.md and set default replay sampling to 0.5% with operator override. Added dashboard alert if replay backlog grows > 5k requests.
Jonah Brooks: Tests are thorough; one nit — snapshot_store restore should validate checksum before applying to runtime to avoid corrupt KV states.
Maya Chen: Added checksum validation and test coverage for snapshot restore paths.
release_notes: Adds session-aware canaries with deterministic shadow replay to validate candidate models against live traffic in a replayed, reproducible way. Enables safer promotions for stateful applications. Operator flag and small migration required.
